Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire. Below are concise answers; I attached a redlined DPA and a data flow diagram (redwood-data-flow-v2.png) for your team. If you prefer a walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute session.

Answers (matching the sheet rows):
1) Storage location and backups:
- Hosted API: customer request content and generated outputs are stored in the region selected at account creation (we currently support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1). Backups are stored in the same region by default; we do not copy production backups automatically to a different region unless the customer enables cross-region DR.
- Private/Dedicated: data remains in customer-managed VPCs or on-premises as configured; Redwood control plane metadata may be stored in our control region (US) with minimal identifiers.

2) Subprocessors with access to raw request content:
- Subprocessors that may access raw request content are limited and include: cloud provider compute/storage for inference (e.g., AWS EC2/EBS/EFS where configured), cloud logging for optional observability pipelines (if enabled), and our managed GPU pool operators for Dedicated customers. A full, current list is at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Credwood-privacy (we update this monthly).
- We maintain contractual controls and limited RBAC on logs. For Hosted customers requiring stricter isolation, we offer Dedicated and Private options and an option to opt out of diagnostic logging.

3) Cross-border transfers & legal mechanisms:
- Default: For Hosted accounts provisioned in EU regions, data remains in-region. For transfers outside the EU, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) supplemented by technical and organizational measures. Where customers require an alternative (e.g., data localization), Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended.
- We also evaluate adequacy decisions; when an adequacy decision exists for the destination, we apply that assessment rather than SCCs. Summary of our approach is attached (scc-and-exports-summary.docx).

4) Customer-controlled keys (BYOK):
- BYOK is available for Private deployments and Dedicated with enterprise commitment. For Hosted API customers we provide envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS by default; we offer a managed bring-your-own-key path for Hosted on a case-by-case basis (requires additional controls and contract terms).

5) Data flow diagram and retention/deletion:
- Attached: redwood-data-flow-v2.png shows ingestion -> runtime -> KV/short-term cache -> optional persistent logs -> telemetry plane.
- Retention: default request logs retained 30 days; customers can configure log retention or request immediate deletion via the Data Deletion API. Deletion requests are processed within 7 business days for Hosted accounts; Private deployments follow customer policies.

6) Access controls & least privilege:
- Internal access is role-based and audited. Sensitive logs and PII are only accessible to a small operations group under break-glass procedures; all access requires MFA and just-in-time approval for escalation.
- We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and granular IAM roles in the console for customer teams.

7) Evidence and compliance artifacts:
- SOC 2 Type II: available under NDA. Marissa, can you please share the secure link?
- DPA: attached (redwood-dpa-v3.pdf) — includes SCCs in Appendix B.

If you'd like, we can mark any fields in your sheet that we answered and return the file.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — looping in following Laura's helpful answers. Short answers to your follow-ups: 

1) Third-party analytics/monitoring:
- By default, Hosted API does NOT forward raw request payloads to third-party analytics providers. We send anonymized operational metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) to our monitoring stack. If a customer opts into enhanced diagnostic logging (this is opt-in in the console), the logs may be ingested into a managed logging provider — those providers are listed in our subprocessors document. Default retention for operational metrics is 90 days; opt-in diagnostic logs follow the customer's selected retention (default 30 days).

2) BYOK gating and lead time for Hosted:
- Gating: contractual controls (DPA addendum), technical validation (key wrapping and lifecycle tests), and an operational runbook for key rotation/incident response.
- Lead time: typically 4-6 weeks for standard enterprise accounts after contract signature; expedited paths available with Dedicated commitments.

3) SOC 2 access:
- We host the SOC 2 Type II report on a secure portal. Please complete this short access request form and we will provision a one-time view link (link below). The report is available under NDA.

Secure SOC 2 access request: https://redwood-internal.secure-docs.com/request?report=soc2

4) DPA negotiations & turnaround:
- We are open to limited redlines around data handling and export restrictions. Typical legal cycle is 1-2 weeks for straightforward edits; complex enterprise redlines can take 3-4 weeks. We assign a named contract owner for every enterprise deal.

If this is sufficient, I can: (a) return the questionnaire with our answers filled inline, (b) provision SOC 2 access once an NDA is in place, and (c) share a DocuSign link for our standard DPA. Which would you prefer?

Thanks — Marissa
Enterprise Programs, Redwood Inference

Related links: https://redwood-internal.secure-docs.com/request?report=soc2
